title: Tummy Tuck After Ozempic: Timing, Loose Skin and GLP-1s
meta_description: Loose belly skin after Ozempic or another GLP-1? When a tummy tuck makes sense, how long to keep a stable weight, what to tell your surgeon about the drug.
excerpt: GLP-1 weight loss can leave loose skin that exercise can't remove. When a tummy tuck makes sense, how long to wait at a stable weight, what current guidance and recent studies say about the drug before surgery, and what recovery looks like.
quick_answer:
Can you get a tummy tuck after Ozempic?

Yes, once your weight settles. A tummy tuck removes loose skin left by GLP-1 weight loss, but be close to your goal weight for 6 to 12 months (Paul Vitenas, MD, on the ASPS website). Tell your surgeon and anesthesia team: 2024 multi-society guidance suggests most patients stay on it, but some surgeons ask for a pause.

sources.title: Understanding how medications interact with anesthesia and when to stop before plastic surgery
quotes: "Most anesthesiologists require patients to stop weight loss medications for at least two to three weeks prior to general anesthesia," said ASPS Member Surgeon Anna Steve, MD .

Dr. Steve also noted that some surgeons may ask patients to hold off on taking their weight loss medications for a specific period following surgery so they can optimize the nutrition available for optimal wound healing.

"Anesthesiologists have found that the way these drugs work is that they keep you feeling full for longer because they slow digestion," said Dr. Preminger. "When digestion gets slowed, your stomach stays full for longer and when you go to sleep for surgery, it puts you at increased risk for aspiration. Aspiration is when the contents of your stomach come up and go into your lungs."
Aspiration can cause serious complications including pneumonia, lung damage and even death.
